Creamy Chicken Potato Soup

ByÁjọkẹPublished: October 8, 2026
No ratings yet

Instaread

This creamy chicken and potato soup is thick, cosy and comforting, with tender chunks of potato, shredded chicken, carrots and celery in a creamy chicken broth. Part of the cooked potatoes and carrots are blended and stirred back into the soup, giving it a lovely creamy texture without needing loads of cream. This is truly a warm hug in a bowl. Serve it with warm crusty bread or cheese on toast for the ultimate comfort food.

Try my potato corn chowder and creamy chicken tortellini soup next.

Why you will love this recipe

Can we talk about how easy this chicken potato soup is to make? It is cosy enough for colder evenings but, honestly, I would happily eat this any time of the year.

The soup is creamy and thick without being overly rich. My trick is to scoop out some of the cooked potatoes and carrots, blend them until smooth and stir them back into the pot. You get that creamy consistency without adding lots of cream.

It is also a great way to use leftover cooked chicken and potatoes, and there isn’t much prep involved. You can even add leftover bacon if you have some. I also love that everything cooks in one pot and there is very little hands-on work involved, which makes this a good one for busy weeknights.

What you will need

Cooked chicken: Shredded or chopped leftover roast or rotisserie chicken works particularly well for this recipe. You can also use chicken breast or thighs.

Potatoes: Peel and chop them into similar-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

Carrots, celery, and onion: These form the soup’s flavor base.

Chicken stock: I recommend low-sodium stock so you have better control over the seasoning.

Single cream: You only need enough to finish the soup, since the blended vegetables provide most of the creaminess.

Garlic

Unsalted butter and olive oil

Italian seasoning

Parmesan cheese

Lemon juice: Just a squeeze at the end brightens up the creamy broth.

Salt and black pepper

Fresh parsley: For finishing.

How to make creamy chicken potato soup

Place a Dutch oven or large pot over medium-low heat. Add the butter and olive oil, then add the chopped carrots, celery and onion. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften.

Add the garlic and cook briefly until fragrant.

Add the Italian seasoning and chopped potatoes. Stir and cook for another minute or two.

Pour in the chicken stock, season with salt and black pepper and stir to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender.

Remove about 2 cups of the potatoes, carrots and some of the cooking liquid from the pot. Carefully blend until smooth.

Meanwhile, add the cooked chicken to the soup and stir to combine.

Pour the blended vegetables back into the pot, followed by the single cream. Stir well and continue cooking over low heat for another 5 minutes, or until the chicken is heated through and the soup is creamy.

Add the grated Parmesan and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Stir until the cheese has melted, then taste and adjust the salt and black pepper.

Finish with chopped fresh parsley, take the soup off the heat and serve.

Tips

Don’t overdo the cream. Blending some of the potatoes and carrots does most of the work here. Add the cream at the end for richness rather than relying on it to thicken the soup.

Cut the potatoes and carrots to similar sises so they cook evenly. 

Add cooked chicken towards the end. It only needs to heat through. Cooking it for too long can make it dry out.

Adjust the consistency to your liking. If the soup becomes thicker than you want after blending, simply add a little more chicken stock or water.

FAQs

Can I add bacon

Yes. Cook the bacon until crisp, crumble it and stir some into the soup or scatter it over each bowl just before serving.

If you are adding bacon, go easy on the salt until the end. Bacon, chicken stock, and Parmesan all add saltiness to the soup, so taste before adding any extra salt.

Can I make this with fresh chicken

Absolutely. Add the fresh chicken at the same time you add the potatoes, so they boil together. Remove the chicken and shred it, then return it to the pot for the flavors to meld together.

What to serve with the creamy chicken potato soup

I like serving this with buttered crusty bread or protein bread for dipping into the creamy broth. It is so good!

And if you’re feeling a little extra, serve it with air fryer cheese on toast. The crisp bread and melted cheese are very good with this soup.

How to store

Allow the soup to cool before transferring it to an airtight container. Store in the fridge for up to 4 days.

The soup will thicken as it sits because of the potatoes. When reheating, add a splash of chicken stock or water to loosen it, then heat gently on the stove or in the microwave until piping hot throughout.

Creamy Chicken and Potato Soup

Ájọkẹ
This creamy chicken and potato soup is thick, cozy and comforting, with tender chunks of potato, shredded chicken, carrots and celery in a creamy chicken broth. Part of the cooked potatoes and carrots are blended and stirred back into the soup, giving it a lovely creamy texture without needing loads of cream. This is truly a warm hug in a bowl.

Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 10 minutes mins
Cook Time 35 minutes mins
Total Time 45 minutes mins
Course Main Course
Cuisine American, British
Servings 6
Calories 455 kcal

Ingredients
  

  • 650 g potato peeled, cubed into similar sizes
  • 500 g cooked chicken shredded or cubed
  • 2 Tablespoons unsalted butter
  • 1 Tablespoon olive oil
  • 3 medium carrots diced
  • 3 celery ribs diced 1 cup
  • 1 cup Onion finely chopped
  • 5 cups chicken stock
  • 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning
  • 1 cup half and half Single cream
  • 4 garlic cloves finely chopped
  • 1 cup parmesan cheese grated
  • Juice of 1 lemon
  • Salt and black pepper to taste
  • Fresh parsley to serve
Prevent your screen from going dark

Instructions
 

  • Place a Dutch oven or large pot over medium-low heat. Add the butter and olive oil, then add the chopped carrots, celery and onion. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften.
  • Add the garlic and cook briefly until fragrant.
  • Add the Italian seasoning and chopped potatoes. Stir and cook for another minute or two.
  • Pour in the chicken stock, season with salt and black pepper and stir to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender.
  • Remove about 2 cups of the potatoes, carrots and some of the cooking liquid from the pot. Carefully blend until smooth.
  • Meanwhile, add the cooked chicken to the soup and stir to combine.
  • Pour the blended vegetables back into the pot, followed by the single cream. Stir well and continue cooking over low heat for another 5 minutes, or until the chicken is heated through and the soup is creamy.
  • Add the grated Parmesan and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Stir until the cheese has melted, then taste and adjust the salt and black pepper.
  • Finish with chopped fresh parsley, take the soup off the heat and serve.
